articles.title: Israel’s Saied Abu Farchi sent off for corner flag celebration in defeat by Austria
articles.summary: Forward gets second yellow card after equalising. Nations League match ends in 3-1 loss for Israel. Israel’s forward Saied Abu Farchi was ⁠sent off as a result of his goal celebration against Austria in ⁠his side’s 3-1 ​Nations League defeat on Thursday.
body: Abu Farchi headed home in the 55th ⁠minute to bring Israel level after ​Austria had ‌taken the lead ‌through a Romano Schmid penalty before ‌half-time at the Raiffeisen Arena in Linz.

The 20-year-old ran to the corner flag, grabbed it and went down on one knee before continuing his celebration. Some reports suggested Abu Farchi used the corner flag to simulate a gun but he appeared to be mimicking a snooker cue. He has previously posted on social media: “It’s all a celebration of snooker.”
The ‌referee had booked Abu Farchi four minutes earlier and showed ​him a second yellow card for the celebration, leaving Israel with 10 players.
Austria regained ⁠the lead in the 90th minute through ​Phillipp ​Mwene, who scored via Paul ​Wanner’s cross. ‌Sasa Kalajdzic ​added ​a third in stoppage time with a close-range finish.

articles.title: Leeds and Warrington tussle for Grand Final spot
articles.summary: Ahead of the their Super League play-off semi-final, Leeds Rhinos and Warrington Wolves are aiming to assert themselves back at rugby league's top table.
body: Off the back of a bye week courtesy of their second-placed finish, Leeds welcome Warrington on Friday for the first of two play-off semi-finals.

But with St Helens, Wigan and Hull KR taking it in turns to dominate the domestic stage over the best part of the past decade, can two of the titans of the game muscle in on the party and seal the first spot in 3 October's Super League Grand Final?
Leeds come into the fixture following two losses against Wigan and Hull FC at home.
Looking further back, they closed out their regular campaign with three defeats in five matches.

articles.title: Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii given nod to start on wing for Wallabies against South Africa
articles.summary: Versatile player joins Tom Wright and Max Jorgensen in back three. Len Ikitau shifts to outside centre with Hunter Paisami at inside centre. The Wallabies will start rugby league recruit Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii on the wing for the first time in a new-look backfield for Sunday’s Test against the…
body: It is one of two surprises in the selection by coach Les Kiss, who also named six forwards on his bench in a bid to match the power of the world champions.

Suaalii, who has previously been moved to the wing during Wallabies matches but has never started there, will line up on the left, with Max Jorgensen on the opposite wing and fullback Tom Wright in between.

Australia are unbeaten in Kiss’s four matches as coach, but the side has yet to meet one of the traditional rugby powers. The match against the Springboks is also the last before the one-year countdown to the home World Cup begins.

Kiss said playing against the top team in world rugby “focuses the mind” and the team has relished the preparation. “We’ve had a solid preparation window here in Perth ahead of what’s going to be a massive Test against South Africa,” he said.

body: Atlanta (1-2) erased an early 7-0 deficit by scoring 27 straight points to take control amid a chorus of boos at Lambeau Field. The Falcons outrushed the Packers 242 yards to 17.

Green Bay (1-2) lost a home opener for the first time since falling 30-22 to the San Francisco 49ers in 2012. The Packers had won 13 straight home openers from 2013-25 to share the NFL record with the Miami Dolphins, who also won 13 in a row from 1976-88.

Penix went 18 of 25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and an interception in his first action since tearing the ACL in his left knee during a loss to Carolina on 16 November. Atlanta (1-2) had struggled to produce any offense whatsoever with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback the first two weeks of the season.
Robinson and Drake London became the first teammates to each compile at least 150 yards from scrimmage against the Packers at Lambeau Field. London caught nine passes for 194 yards.

articles.title: FA Cup qualifying tie to be replayed after ref's error
articles.summary: Mulbarton Wanderers are "deeply upset" after being told they must replay their FA Cup qualifying tie with Woodford Town because of a referee's error.
body: Mulbarton won 2-1 at Essex Senior League side Woodford in the second qualifying round on Saturday but the home team then lodged a protest with the Football Association following a decision in the 30th minute.
Woodford scored a penalty but the referee disallowed the goal for encroachment by a number of Woodford players and awarded Mulbarton an indirect free-kick.
Law 14 in the laws of the game, external states that the referee should have ordered the penalty to be retaken.
The FA initially said that a protest for misapplication of the rules was not permissible.

articles.title: 'Bosh', backlash and rebuild - how far can Fisher go?
articles.summary: British heavyweight Johnny Fisher - who returns to the Copper Box for his Zuffa Boxing debut on Saturday - reflects on defeat, fame and his rebuild.
body: When Johnny Fisher steps back inside the Copper Box Arena on Saturday night, the surroundings will feel familiar, even if much around his career has changed.

The east London venue was once something of a fortress for Fisher, where John Denver's 'Take Me Home, Country Roads' accompanied his ring walk and thousands of supporters reacted to every punch as his unbeaten record grew.
That changed last year when Dave Allen stopped him in the fifth round, handing the heavyweight his first professional defeat and leading critics to question his standing in the division.
Now the 27-year-old returns to headline against Belgium's Michael Pirotton in a 10-round contest which also marks his promotional debut for Dana White's Zuffa Boxing.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership crowds break four million mark
articles.summary: Scottish Premiership crowds topped four million for the first time last season as the league continues to attract the highest per capita attendances in Europe.
body: From a 4.1m total, average gates in the top flight reached 17,903, up by 3%, as Celtic defended their title thanks to a dramatic final-day victory at home to challengers Hearts.
Only England, Germany, Spain, Italy, France and the Netherlands attracted bigger audiences overall.
Adjusting average crowds for population puts Scotland way out in front with close to 20 attendees per 1,000 residents, nearly twice the figure for the next best nation, Norway.

Figures published by Uefa show approximately six million Scottish supporters watched men's matches during the 2025-26 campaign, with 900,000 in the lower leagues, 200,000 at domestic cup ties and 800,000 at European matches.

articles.title: How USC QB Jayden Maiava helped Jacob Maiava thrive in first UCF football start
articles.summary: With an injury to Owen Spell forcing a shuffle on the UCF Knights' offensive line, redshirt freshman Jacob Maiava earned his first start at center.
body: ORLANDO — Jacob Maiava had plenty of support to settle his nerves before making his first UCF start.

The 6-foot-2, 280-pound redshirt freshman leaned upon the veterans to have his back and depend on him to call the shots at center. He soaked up information from the Knights ' coaching staff, blocking out concerns of asking a "stupid" question.
And when he returned home from practice each day, he called his brother — USC starting quarterback Jayden Maiava — for reassurance and perspective.

"He gave me a FaceTime call and told me to be prepared, to trust the eye in the sky," Maiava said in a phone interview with The News-Journal. "That meant a lot coming from him because he's been through it.

articles.title: Chelsea in landmark fertility policy: 'Being a player and mum are both possible now'
articles.summary: Chelsea are used to being the first. While plenty of that has come on the pitch, it is the behind the scenes work that is truly leading the way for female players and women's health.
body: Now, the Blues are the first team in the WSL to introduced new fertility and maternity policies, giving their players the choice to start a family in whichever way they want to, and the post-natal support to balance the demands of elite sport and motherhood.

The Blues were also the first club in the world to starting tracking menstrual cycles - introduced by Emma Hayes in February 2020 - and how they impact performance. This is the next step in that process.

Chelsea have partnered with Fertility Plus - one of London's leading fertility clinics - to set up a fund accessible to all players in support of their fertility journey. This includes egg freezing, IVF, smear tests and contraception, as well as counselling and workshops to give players everything they need to make informed choices It is not an enforced policy and players can access it however they need with support from Chelsea.

articles.title: Florida woman places in UCI Gran Fondo World Championship in Japan
articles.summary: A Treasure Coast woman traveled to Niseko, Japan, to compete in the 2026 UCI Gran Fondo World Championships and came back with a second place medal. Karla Antonio, 56, of Stuart, placed second in the women's 55-59 time trial. The competition was Aug.
body: The competition was Aug. 26-30 and had four different races: road race Gran Fondo 140 kilometer, road race Medio Fondo 80 kilometer, time trial, and team relay. In the time trial, racers start individually instead of all at once.

"In a way, it's almost more stressful because you have no idea if anyone else is going faster than you," Antonio told TCPalm. "You have no idea, you just have to go as hard as you can go — the whole way."
Antonio started doing triathlons when she was 18. Initially more of a runner, she ran in college and competitively after college. About six years ago, she made the switch to just cycling.
"I entered the state time trial race and was completely thrilled I got third," she said. "Looking back on it now, in six years I went from third in Florida to second in the world."

articles.title: 'Exploitative ideas' - Top leagues criticise Infantino and call for FIFA reform
articles.summary: A joint statement from Europe's top leagues has hit out at "exploitative ideas" pushed by FIFA president Gianni Infantino and called for "essential" reform of football's governing body.
body: This summer, Infantino was forced to abandon a plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup after a backlash which led to UEFA pursuing legal action.

Earlier this week, in a letter to FIFA members, Infantino said he was open to an independent external review of the plan and that he should be allowed to continue leading FIFA because his responsibilities are "larger than any individual proposal or disagreement". There will be a FIFA presidential election in March 2027.

However, the Premier League, Bundesliga, LaLiga and Serie A chiefs have now called for "a new governance structure for our sport's global governing body that is transparent, objective, proportionate and inclusive".

"Football's longstanding foundations have, in recent years, been threatened by a fundamental governance problem, whereby FIFA's president has actively promoted exploitative ideas rather than safeguarding against them," the leagues say.
